basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 11.' and it opens '(Cap. XLIII.—Vers. 11.) Et deferte viro munera, aliquid resinae, et mellis, thymiama et'. Migne prints the chapter at the head of this block.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XLIII.—Vers. 11.) Et deferte viro munera, aliquid resinae, et mellis, thymiama et stacten, et terebinthum, et nuces. Sive, ut Aquila et Symmachus transtulerunt, amygdala. Idcirco hoc capitulum posuimus, ut sciamus ubi in nostris codicibus habetur thymiama, in Hebraeo esse NECOTHA (נכאת), quod Aquila storacem transtulit. Ex quo domus nechota, quae in Isaia (XXXIX, 21) legitur, manifestissime cella thymiamatis, sive storacis intelligitur, quod in illa aromata diversa sint condita.
